method: Read-only copy of latest user world snapshot; region cache seeded from earlier profiling copy. Main game terrain/clearance pipeline runs normally; train simulation, camera motion, track mesh rebuilding and train UI paused to isolate terrain editing. Four cases after initial settling; 0.4 s edit debounce included in elapsed. Moving one parallel-group node modifies eight segment preparations in this layout. CPU timings only, no GPU measurement. Worker totals are summed concurrent work and must not be added to elapsed. One event can disappear from p99; inspect main-thread max per event. Two runs gave similar main stalls and worker delays. No terrain algorithm/behavior optimizations made.
findings: Main-thread affected-chunk search causes about 133-146 ms stalls by checking old and new earthwork fields over all candidate chunks, including expensive natural-height sampling.

Every earthwork update marks all chunks touched by any track as affected, instead of only chunks changed by the edit: 31 submissions/replacements for an eight-segment group edit, with only three generated meshes. An unchanged notification also replaces 31 chunks while generating none.
Three chunk builds run concurrently, but adaptive vertex/normal/color generation and stitching takes most worker time; building three meshes delays completion about five to six seconds.
Earthwork preparation on one worker takes about 170 ms including full-field BVH reconstruction. Parallelizing preparation alone would not fix the main-thread stall or multi-second mesh latency.

Uploads are a smaller cost: roughly 50 ms total spread over 31 uploads, usually under 5 ms per frame for the upload scope. Region cache avoids regenerating 28 unchanged meshes but still reads, decodes and uploads them. Repeating a raised state after restoring can miss the region cache because the latest per-key signature replaces the previous one.
recommended_order: Compute dirty bounds from changed/removed prepared paths, skip unchanged updates, and pass affected keys to the main thread instead of sampling heights across all resident chunks.
Keep unchanged chunk meshes and tree clearance entries mounted; avoid disk reads, decoding and uploading unchanged geometry.
Profile/cache repeated natural and earthwork height samples in adaptive mesh generation; preserve exact geometry, normals and colors.
Only then assess parallel changed-segment preparation and more incremental BVH updates.

changes: Compare changed and removed controls against the last applied snapshot, not an obsolete completed job.
Skip field rebuild and invalidation for unchanged snapshots.
Resolve changed old/new path coverage and chunk identities on a worker. Main thread uses resolved flags, with conservative coverage for chunks that arrived during computation.
Keep unchanged mounted meshes, cached LODs, tree batches and unaffected in-flight chunk results.
Bounded per-chunk exact natural/resolved height memoization: at most 65,536 entries per dictionary.
Stitch leaf fans using bounded sorted-set intervals instead of scanning whole rows/columns.

Dirty bounds include the widest old/new shoulder influence; cache signatures include nearby nearest-path competitors and coarse mesh decisions. This fixes masked wide-embankment dependencies; existing saves remain compatible, with affected old cache records regenerated on demand.
local_invalidation_optimization.method: Same copied save, node, camera, settings and harness as baseline. Additional superseded edit/undo case. 0.4 s debounce included. CPU Debug/headless; no GPU performance claim. Terrain height/slope formulas and triangle winding remain unchanged; cache identities now include nearest-path competitors. Timings include scheduling and GC noise; comparison is a local diagnostic, not a large-world guarantee.
tests: Original terrain fixtures: vertex/triangle counts, triangle index hashes, vertex heights, normals and colors.
Local coverage checks for wide cuts/fills, deletions, tree clearance, adaptive topology and chunks arriving during a worker job.
Unchanged and superseded edit/undo produce zero chunk submissions or mesh replacements.
Unrelated cached LODs and in-flight chunks survive revisions; stale affected jobs remain rejected.
Deleting a narrow path exposes a distant wide-embankment area: both invalidation and disk cache identity change correctly.
